QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_11

question.text: As an AIF Manager positioning your Category I VC fund to a potential UHNI LP, which of the following is the STRONGEST portfolio-diversification argument specifically for AIF assets within an HNI's overall portfolio?

answer.text: AIF assets guarantee positive returns uncorrelated with public markets due to SEBI regulatory backing
AIF assets have daily NAV, high liquidity and low fees, making them superior to mutual funds on every dimension
AIF assets are fully hedged against market beta by mandate, eliminating systematic risk from the portfolio

AIF assets provide exposure to high-growth unlisted equity, real estate debt, infrastructure and special-situation products that are not available through on-market investing, offering diversification and upside alpha opportunities

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that AIF assets — such as high-growth unlisted equity and debt, real estate and infrastructure, special situations, structured debt, and Category III derivative products — offer opportunities that are not available in on-market investing. This access-plus-diversification argument is the core portfolio rationale for AIF allocations within an HNI's overall portfolio. The Trap: Option A falsely promises "guaranteed positive returns" — no such regulatory backing exists. Option B is wrong on liquidity (AIFs are illiquid) and fees (AIF fees are higher than mutual funds). Option C overstates beta neutralisation — only specific market-neutral strategies aim at this, and even then not fully. Option D is the supported answer. Note: The earlier trap section mislabelled the options and incorrectly said Option D was wrong. The labels have been corrected so that B carries the liquidity/fees error, C carries the beta-neutralisation error, and D is identified as the supported answer.
